He co-leads the Dementia Research Group at Oxford University and serves as editor-in-chief of Brain, one of the most respected journals in neurology. context.real_quote: For David, the effort of putting the music systems together was not worth the reward of being able to listen to something pleasurable — and in David's case, very few things were worth the effort.
key_stats: People who develop apathy in older age have twice the chance of developing dementia in the next 10 years compared to those with normal motivation (Oxford University / Dementia Research Group research)
The basal ganglia are approximately 360 million years old, evolutionarily preserved across species to link motivational cues to action
David's two strokes occurred in the deep basal ganglia and were only visible on high-resolution scans, not standard imaging
David was treated with Ropinirole and returned transformed — new job, new girlfriend — within 3 months
Approximately one third of people with depression do not respond to serotonergic antidepressants (treatment-resistant depression), according to Dr. Husain
There are over 200 causes of dementia, of which Alzheimer's disease is the most common

pending_qa.q: What is the difference between Alzheimer's disease and dementia?
pending_qa.r: Dr. Husain explains that dementia is a broad clinical definition referring to a progressive change in a person where cognitive or behavioral impairment begins to affect everyday life — it has over 200 distinct causes. Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause of dementia, characterized by the buildup of proteins called amyloid and tau, which have toxic effects on neurons. The location in the brain where this pathology accumulates determines whether the first symptoms are memory-related, motivation-related, or behavioral.

pending_qa.q: Are there genetic causes of Alzheimer's disease, and do they run in families?
pending_qa.r: Dr. Husain acknowledges that there are unusual genetic causes of Alzheimer's disease that run in families, involving mutations in genes called presenilin 1, presenilin 2, or amyloid precursor protein — all of which affect amyloid, the protein that builds up in the brain. These genetic mutations tend to cause early-onset Alzheimer's. However, he notes that for most cases of Alzheimer's, which is a very common disease of aging, there is no clear familial inheritance pattern of the type that would make a direct parent-to-child prediction reliable.
